response.title: how long do whole house battery backup systems last
response.answer:
Whole-house battery backup systems typically last 10–20 years before needing replacement, but how long they can power your house during an outage is a different question.

There are three important ways to measure battery lifespan:

1. Battery lifespan (years)

Battery type

	

Typical lifespan

	

Common warranty




Lithium iron phosphate (LFP)

	

15–20 years

	

10–15 years




Lithium nickel manganese cobalt (NMC)

	

10–15 years

	

10 years




Lead-acid

	

3–7 years

	

1–5 years

Modern home battery systems increasingly use LFP chemistry because of its long cycle life and thermal stability.

A 10-year warranty doesn't mean the battery stops working after 10 years. It usually means the manufacturer guarantees a certain amount of remaining battery capacity, often around 60–70%, subject to warranty conditions.

2. How long can they power your house during an outage?

This depends on battery capacity and your home's electricity consumption.

Assuming a 27 kWh battery system with approximately 24 kWh of usable energy:

Average household load

	

Backup duration




0.5 kW (essential loads)

	

48 hours




1 kW (light usage)

	

24 hours




2 kW (moderate usage)

	

12 hours




4 kW (heavy usage, AC)

	

6 hours

Air conditioning, electric heating, EV charging, and electric water heaters can dramatically shorten backup duration.

With solar panels, a battery can potentially sustain your home through multi-day outages if solar generation is sufficient to recharge it.

3. What determines how many years the system lasts?

The biggest factors are:

Charge cycles: Daily charging and discharging causes more wear than occasional outage-only use.

Temperature: Batteries kept in moderate temperatures generally last longer.

Depth of discharge: Repeatedly draining a battery completely can accelerate degradation.

Battery chemistry: LFP generally offers better cycle life than NMC.

For financial planning, I would use 10–15 years as the expected replacement interval, with 15–20 years as a possible longer-life outcome rather than a guarantee. 
Clean Energy Group
+2

One question: Are you asking how many years the battery system lasts before replacement, or how many hours/days it can run your entire house during a power outage?

The answer is quite different, especially if you want to run central air conditioning.
